title: A Phone-Free Evening
text: Last month, Omar noticed that his family rarely talked during dinner. Everyone brought a phone to the table, and somebody was always checking a message or watching a short video. Omar suggested a simple experiment: the family would leave their phones in a drawer during dinner for one week. At first, his younger sister complained because she was waiting for an important reply from a friend. His father worried that a work call might arrive, but he agreed to try. The first evening felt strange. Without their screens, they finished eating quickly and sat in silence. Then Omar asked his father about a photograph on the wall, and the conversation became easier. By the end of the week, they were telling stories, discussing plans, and laughing more often. They did not decide to stop using technology. Instead, they created a quiet hour each evening and kept phones away from the table. The experiment showed them that a small rule could change the way they spent time together. They still used online calendars and sent messages, but they chose different moments for those activities. Omar wrote the rule on a card and placed it beside the drawer, where everybody could see it. After a month, nobody wanted to remove the card.
